To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

during PC12-cell apoptosis induced by serum deprivation and nerve growth factor deprivation, (1) [32P]phosphate uptake is decreased and (2) [32P]-phosphate incorporation into tau and high-mol-wt tau is increased.

(a) energy metabolism is maintained during apoptosis; (b) protein phosphorylation is increased during apoptosis and may be important for the execution of this death process; and (c) phosphorylation of tau is preferentially enhanced during neuronal apoptosis.
during apoptosis of neuronal cells, phosphate uptake is decreased, ATP levels are maintained at control levels and phosphorylation of tau protein increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of apoptosis and the role of specific protein-phosphorylated events during this death process.
the regulation of protein phosphorylation in neuronal PC12 cells during apoptosis, and the role that energy metabolism may play in this regulation.
the regulation of protein phosphorylation during neuronal apoptosis and the role of protein phosphorylation in the regulation of apoptosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

during apoptosis of differentiated PC12 cells, energy metabolism and phosphate uptake were decreased significantly, and protein phosphorylations were increased in the presence of a maintained ATP level.
, during neuronal PC12-cell death by apoptosis, energy metabolism and [32P] incorporation into ATP are decreased.

the decrease in Na+-stimulated phosphate uptake during apoptosis may be a result of a decreased Na+-K+-ATPase activity, and that a decrease in the incorporation of [32Phosphate]Pi into ATP may be due to the decrease in Na +-stimulated phosphate uptake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the apoptotic process is an active, energy-dependent process in which specific proteins are phosphorylated in a regulated manner.
the decrease in phosphate uptake and ATP synthesis during apoptosis may be compensated by a preferential phosphorylated protein pool.
, in neuronal PC12 cells, the apoptotic process involves an increased phosphorylation of specific protein(s) in a phosphate-dependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the energy metabolism and protein-phosphorylated events during apoptosis are different from those of normal cells, and these events may play an important and specific role in the regulation and execution of apoptosis.
during apoptosis, [ 32 P]Pi incorporation into proteins is preferential, with tau and HMW-tau phosphorylation being increased.
protein phosphorylation is not a general process during apoptosis but is specific to certain proteins, including the tau proteins.
